title: Equinor and VNG sign 18-year gas sales agreement for supplies to Germany
summary: Equinor will supply natural gas to the German energy company VNG until the end of 2044.
body_markdown:
Under the agreement, Equinor will deliver up to 15.3 TWh (around 1.4 billion cubic metres – bcm) of natural gas per year to VNG. Deliveries will start on 1 January 2027 and continue until the end of 2044, with gas delivered at Trading Hub Europe, the German gas market area. Pricing will reflect market terms, while other commercial details are confidential between the parties.


“This milestone agreement with VNG demonstrates the continued demand for long-term gas supplies in Europe. Building on our long-standing partnership and reliable production from the Norwegian continental shelf, Equinor is well positioned to meet this demand and contribute to Europe’s energy security for years to come”, says Anders Opedal, president and CEO of Equinor.


The commercial team from Equinor and VNG


Photo: Ole Jørgen Bratland / ©Equinor


For VNG, the agreement represents a significant milestone in securing long-term gas supplies for customers in Germany. VNG and Equinor have a relationship dating back several decades. The first natural gas deliveries from Norway to eastern Germany took place in 1996, and the new agreement builds on this established cooperation.


“Norwegian pipeline gas continues to play an important role in ensuring a secure energy supply for Germany and Europe. With this long-term contract we are deepening our successful partnership with Equinor and supporting our customers with a reliable and comparatively low-emission gas supply,” says Ulf Heitmüller, CEO of VNG AG.


The agreement between VNG Handel & Vertrieb GmbH (VNG H&V), a wholly owned subsidiary of VNG AG, and Equinor was signed in Oslo on 24 November by Ulf Heitmüller, chair of the executive board of VNG AG, and Anders Opedal, president and CEO of Equinor. The tenor of 18 years is the longest for any agreement for sales of gas from Norway since the Troll agreements in 1986.


Germany is Equinor’s largest market for natural gas and has been an anchor market for Norwegian gas since exports started in 1977.


Natural gas is expected to remain a key part of Europe’s energy mix as more renewable power and low carbon solutions are developed. Norwegian gas production is among the lowest-emission operations in the international gas industry, and pipeline supply from the Norwegian continental shelf benefits from electrification of platforms and onshore processing plants combined with short transport distances to the continent.
